source.title: Better artificial intelligence does not mean better models of biology
source.authors: Drew A. Linsley; Pin-Yuan Feng; Thomas Serre

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports results on how well vision models align with primate neural responses and human feature-importance maps, not on whether different models become more similar to one another.
record.gate_note: The paper measures model-to-biology alignment, a related but different construct from model-to-model representational convergence. Its own reported findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Findings attributed to cited work, including the reported effects of Harmonization, are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures how well vision DNNs predict primate ITC responses and human feature-importance maps. That is model-to-biology alignment. It reports no model-to-model, cross-modal, cross-seed, mapping or shared-feature similarity, so its results bear on no version. It cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis [125] once, in passing, for the speculation that the 'right' data and objective could yield biological strategies. That is a citation, not a discussion or test, so the relation is cites_only rather than discusses.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that DNN alignment with primate vision has plateaued or worsened as models reach human-level accuracy, likely because the models use different visual strategies. They argue that vision science should develop biologically grounded data diets and learning principles rather than rely on AI benchmark progress.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not test the original model-to-model representation-similarity methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported relation between ImageNet accuracy and biological alignment differs across accuracy groups and changes around the stated changepoints.

fits_no_version.finding: In Brain-Score, ITC predictivity rose with ImageNet accuracy up to about 70% accuracy (about half the neural variance explained), then declined. The changepoint model was VOneGRCNN-52e-full (Fig. 1A). No row records this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Beyond moderate ImageNet accuracy, more accurate DNNs predict primate ITC responses worse.

fits_no_version.finding: Model-to-brain and model-to-human alignment plateaus or reverses with scale and accuracy. The superhuman EVA-02 was as ITC-aligned as MobileNetV3. This is the record's r1 to r6 findings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher ImageNet accuracy does not imply better alignment with primate neural responses or human feature use.

record.problems: The reported findings concern biological alignment rather than convergence between models. The article gives mainly qualitative trends for the relevant analyses rather than per-model numerical results; some figure uncertainty information is described without corresponding numerical estimates in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported outcomes relevant to model-to-model convergence were found. Results attributed to cited work, including Harmonization outcomes, were not recorded as this paper's own results.

untested.parts: All: no model-to-model alignment is measured across scale or capability.
All: no vision-language paired-data alignment is measured.
All: no cross-model mapping or stitching. Linear fits are to neural data, not to other models.
All: no cross-model feature or circuit comparison.
All: metric and data dependence of model-to-model convergence is not examined.
All: the plateau reported is in model-to-brain alignment, not model-to-model alignment.

record.verdict_notes: All six rows correctly carry versions ['none']. The text names the feature-map changepoint inconsistently: 'adversarially-trained ResNet50' in the body, 'Adversarially-trained Wide ResNet50' in the figure captions. The Fig. 1A Brain-Score trend is unrecorded, but it is model-to-brain and bears on no version. Harmonization results are attributed to prior work [89,113,114], and Harmonization induces alignment deliberately, so excluding them is right.

versions.untested_parts: Whether independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data become more aligned with one another as scale and capability increase.
Whether image and caption representations in vision and language models align more as both models improve.
Whether networks trained from different initializations converge on shared features or subspaces.
Whether representations can be mapped or stitched between models, including with linear or unpaired mappings.
Whether interpretable features or circuits recur across models.
Whether model-to-model convergence depends on similarity metrics, settings, or input data.
Whether model-to-model alignment is incomplete or plateaus, or is explained by shared training data or objectives.
